Liquid-based preparations of urinary cytology have been shown to significantly better evaluate malignant categories and provide more accurate diagnoses compared to classically prepared cases. According to the College of American Pathologists interlaboratory comparison program, liquid-based preparations performed well in several challenges, including evaluating adenocarcinoma and HGUCA (human glomerular podocyte cell) categories. However, there was no significant difference observed for urinary cytology challenges when comparing liquid-based with classically prepared cases.

The performance of liquid-based preparations can be attributed to the increased sensitivity and specificity they offer compared to traditional cytological procedures. This is due to the reduced cell shedding and other factors that may compromise sample quality in classical preparations. The results suggest that liquid-based preparations facilitate a more accurate diagnosis than conventional preparations, making them an essential tool for evaluating urinary cytology samples.

Additionally, the use of liquid-based preparations can provide valuable insights into the molecular characteristics of bladder lesions, including PT injury and tubular lesion assessment. By facilitating non-invasive and sensitive assessments, these procedures can help improve patient outcomes and diagnostic accuracy.
